description.content:
The DynamicProductLiteViewSet provides a way to fetch the list of available products by providing loan request data
 as input since no actual LR will exist at the time of calling this in Advisor Simulator v2.
It is used to select products to add to an offer as product items.

The list is a multiplication of the active ProductVersions with a start date of at least today and
the allowed variabilities configured for the product.
As an example:
2 Products (A & B) with each one version
Product A has 2 allowed variabilities (fix and 5-5-5)
Product B has 1 allowed variabilities (fix)
The view will return 3 results
If product A has 2 versions that have a start date of at least today, the view will return 5 results.

Next to the product details, the view runs the acceptance rules and provides the result in the errors attribute.

Developer notes:
The logic used in this view and its related code assumes that there is no offer or product items
to base calculations on.

You can define the duration you want to calculate the products for by setting the query params min_duration
and max_duration to an equal value. Otherwise, those values are only used to filter and the default duration
on the product version is used in the calculations.,

Inputs will be sent in the body of the POST request:
{
    "loan_amount": decimal,
    "cash_own_funds": decimal,
    "bridge_loan_amount": decimal,
    "realty_price": decimal,
    "building_costs": decimal,
    "price_of_land": decimal,
    "total_renovation_costs": decimal,
    "cost_vat": decimal,
    "additional_financing_needs": decimal,
    "region": {
        "id": int,
        "definition": "str"
    },
    "is_main_first_residence": boolean,
    "venal_value_after": decimal,
    "loan_purposes": [
        {
            "id": int,
            "definition": "str"
        }
    ]
}

As inputs we will take known data from the simulator and construct LoanRequest and Realty objects, which will then
be used to initialize DataHandlers in Serializer context. Then the serializer will proceed with rate calculations.
This serializer won't be running acceptance criteria and will not have the results in the data.

The DynamicProductLiteViewSet provides a way to fetch the list of available products by providing loan request data
 as input since no actual LR will exist at the time of calling this in Advisor Simulator v2.
It is used to select products to add to an offer as product items.

The list is a multiplication of the active ProductVersions with a start date of at least today and
the allowed variabilities configured for the product.
As an example:
2 Products (A & B) with each one version
Product A has 2 allowed variabilities (fix and 5-5-5)
Product B has 1 allowed variabilities (fix)
The view will return 3 results
If product A has 2 versions that have a start date of at least today, the view will return 5 results.

Next to the product details, the view runs the acceptance rules and provides the result in the errors attribute.

Developer notes:
The logic used in this view and its related code assumes that there is no offer or product items
to base calculations on.

You can define the duration you want to calculate the products for by setting the query params min_duration
and max_duration to an equal value. Otherwise, those values are only used to filter and the default duration
on the product version is used in the calculations.,

Inputs will be sent in the body of the POST request:
{
    "loan_amount": decimal,
    "cash_own_funds": decimal,
    "bridge_loan_amount": decimal,
    "realty_price": decimal,
    "building_costs": decimal,
    "price_of_land": decimal,
    "total_renovation_costs": decimal,
    "cost_vat": decimal,
    "additional_financing_needs": decimal,
    "region": {
        "id": int,
        "definition": "str"
    },
    "is_main_first_residence": boolean,
    "venal_value_after": decimal,
    "loan_purposes": [
        {
            "id": int,
            "definition": "str"
        }
    ]
}

As inputs we will take known data from the simulator and construct LoanRequest and Realty objects, which will then
be used to initialize DataHandlers in Serializer context. Then the serializer will proceed with rate calculations.
This serializer won't be running acceptance criteria and will not have the results in the data.
